name: Filter-toolbar-bar
purpose: The control bar that sits above a table, list, grid or chart and DRIVES it: a search field, an add-filter menu, a date-range trigger, a view switch, a results count, a removable applied-filter chip row with a +N overflow, a clear-all, and right-aligned actions (export, density). Composed ENTIRELY from existing gated atoms (Search-field, Dropdown, Segmented-control, Tags, Links) — no new visual vocabulary, only arrangement, state and wiring. Itinerary row 120 (Layer 2). #261 design pass, Dave's nomination: it is the thing that drives a dashboard, so it now carries a documented event/attribute contract instead of being a decorative row of controls.

props.name: density
props.$note: A DIAL, not an assembly (changed at #261): `data-density` on the bar root moves the search/trigger height 48px→40px and the bar padding 12px→8px, both on the 4px grid, both clear of the 24px dial-down floor. The bar also HANDS the same value to its consumer as `data-apollo-density`, which is the point — one control, two surfaces. The old structural reading of this prop (full = arrangement A, compact = arrangement B) is superseded by the `arrangement` prop below, so the two axes stop being conflated.

props.name: arrangement
props.$note: Structural variance (a different assembly — the VARIANTS axis, the reading Tags' own `type` prop carries, s142-D1 class C6). dashboard = the full two-row bar. dense = underline search + one small segmented control, sitting directly above a table/list, no context row.

props.name: filterCount
props.$note: 0-N applied filters. Each is one dismissible Tags chip; the organism draws no new chip.

props.name: chipOverflow
props.$note: How many chips stay visible before the rest collapse behind a `+N more` disclosure. The disclosure is a BUTTON carrying `.tag`, so it takes the chip paint and the chip's own hit floor rather than inventing a control.

props.name: state
props.$note: One attribute, `data-ftb-state`, on the bar root. Every state-scoped node declares the states it belongs to in `data-when`; nodes without `data-when` are always present. The bar does NOT set this from its own optimism — it reads it back off the consumer's `data-apollo-result-state` (see edges.drivesConsumer).

props.name: sticky
props.$note: `position:sticky` under the page header, offset by `--ftb-top` (0 by default). The stuck shadow is EARNED, not permanent: an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel above the bar flips `data-stuck`.

variants.name: dashboard
variants.use: Two rows — controls (search · add filter · date range · view · density · export) and context (results count · applied-filter chips · clear all). The two rows collapse to ONE at a container width of 1180px and above.

variants.name: dense
variants.use: A compact bar directly above a Table/List-items region — underline search + a small segmented control (sort/view), no context row.

states.name: no-filters
states.shows: the total count and a `No filters applied` hint; no chip row, no clear-all.

states.name: filtered
states.shows: `N of M`, the chip row (with `+N more` past the overflow threshold), and clear-all.

states.name: loading
states.shows: a skeleton where the count sits — the count's POSITION is held so the row does not jump — plus the word `Updating results`, announced through `role=status`/`aria-live=polite`/`aria-busy`. Chips dim but stay interactive; the controls are never disabled, because a filter you cannot change while it is running is a trap.

states.name: empty
states.shows: `0 of M`, the chips that produced the zero (so the user can see what to remove), and a message block with a bell glyph, a title, a sentence and a `Clear all filters` action.

states.name: error
states.shows: an em-dash where the count would be — never a stale number presented as fresh — and a message block in rag/error-ink carrying an error triangle AND a text title AND a sentence saying nothing was changed, plus `Try again`. Colour is the third channel, never the only one (1.4.1).

chipStates: removing (max-width collapse, then removed from the DOM and the tab order)
stateModel.$note: The five states are mutually exclusive and CSS-selected; nothing is toggled by script except the one attribute.

tokens.search: form/border/* + form/background/hover via Search-field.reference.html (boxed and underline variants), unmodified
tokens.filters: the full dropdown/menu/listbox token set via Dropdown.reference.html (boxed variant), unmodified
tokens.view: tertiary/background/* + secondary/background/default via Segmented-control.reference.html, unmodified — PROMOTED off View-options (Dave, 2026-07-24)
tokens.chips: form/border/default + the applied-filters container-query collapse via Tags.reference.html, unmodified
tokens.links: text/default underline treatment via Links.reference.html — ONE DECLARED DEVIATION: the source selector is `a.lnk`; clear-all and retry are ACTIONS, so they must be <button> (4.1.2). The selector widens to `:is(a.lnk,button.lnk)` and a button reset plus a 24px centred ::before hit expander are added. The PAINT is unmodified.
tokens.status: rag/error-ink (#DA1A00 light / #F6604C dark) and rag/success-ink (#137F3C / #66CC8D) — the TWO-RED LAW pair, s151-D1. Plus/minus numerals are the only coloured text; the minus sign in the numeral is the declared non-colour carrier (`data-carries="label"`, measured at the browser by _validate_state_contrast.py).
tokens.$note: Every token above resolves through the ATOM's own manifest or the semantic store; this organism binds nothing new. The bar's own CSS (`.ftb-*`) is flex arrangement, container queries and state selection only.

responsive.$status: PROPOSED at #261 (not ruled) — reflow driven in headless Chromium at 1240 / 680 / 375 px.
responsive.rule: Container >=1180px: ONE row — controls left, results count + chips + clear-all right. 680-1180px: two rows, the context row beneath the controls. <=680px: the search claims its own full-width row and the actions unpin from the right. <=400px (375px phone, WCAG 1.4.10 reachable to 320px): every control stacks full-width, the segmented groups go full width with flex:1 buttons, and the chip row collapses to one-chip-per-row at <=360px via Tags' OWN unmodified container query. No horizontal scroll at any width.
responsive.$note: s210-D3 discipline: the bar declares no width of its own; the container gives it one. Every breakpoint is a CONTAINER query, so the bar reflows correctly inside a bento tile (s248-D3).

livesInside: Page (above a Table, Data-grid, List-items or chart region)
commonPatterns: compact sort bar above a table
filter bar driving a data grid

behaviour.fallback: JS off: every control still paints and still takes focus — the search input types, the three dropdown triggers are real buttons, the two segmented groups keep the `aria-pressed` the markup authors, the chips the markup authors stay, and the results count reads the number the markup authors. What goes: the search clear button does nothing, the menus never open (`aria-expanded` stays false, `data-open` stays false), the segmented indicator never leaves its authored position, chips cannot be dismissed, the +N overflow never expands, and no `apollo:filter-*` event is emitted — so the consumer keeps the unfiltered set the server rendered. The bar degrades to an honest, inert description of the current query, never to a lying one.

$note.composition: Five unedited borrowings kept in step with their sources — Search-field (clear), Dropdown (open/choose/outside-click close), Segmented-control (indicator placement, re-placed on resize), Tags (chip dismiss) and Links (paint only, no script) — plus the toolbar's OWN driver written under s258-D1.
$note.dropdownHook: `wireDD` takes ONE added argument, an `onChoose(option, valueSpan)` hook. Returning false means 'do not latch' — used by the add-filter and export menus, which are ACTION menus (they emit and reset) rather than SELECTION menus. The borrowed body is otherwise untouched.
$note.dismiss: The Tags dismiss carries the #218 lane cB repair verbatim: the transitionend listener is NOT {once:true} and unsubscribes only on its own propertyName, with a 600ms fallback timer so the removal can never depend on an event that may not fire; focus moves to the next remaining dismiss, or to the group. It is now a reusable `wireDismiss(x, after)` because chips are created at runtime.
$note.resize: EXACTLY ONE window resize listener on the page, rAF-debounced with cancelAnimationFrame (ADR-0015). It re-places the segmented indicators.
$note.budget: No network, no setInterval, no external script src. The one setTimeout is the dismiss fallback timer, not polling.

accessibility.structure: The bar is a `<form role="search">` with an accessible name. Search-field keeps its own type="search"/aria-label; Dropdown keeps its own role="combobox"/listbox/option triad; Segmented-control keeps its own role="group"+aria-pressed; Tags keeps its own aria-label per dismiss button; the chip row is a named `role="group"`. The results count is a `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` region, and carries `aria-busy` while loading — so a filter change is ANNOUNCED, not merely repainted (4.1.3).
accessibility.focus: Every borrowed atom keeps its OWN :focus-visible ring. The two added button seats — `button.lnk` and the `+N more` chip — take the Links inset underline and the Tags focus ring respectively; neither is a new focus style. Dismissing a chip moves focus to the next remaining dismiss, or to the chip group (2.4.3).
accessibility.targets: Driven at 1240/680/375px by _validate_hit_area.py: 54 targets measured per width, ZERO below the 24px dial-down floor (s116-D1). The 24px seats are Tags' own `.x`, Search-field's own `.clear`, and the added `button.lnk`, whose visible cap-height run is grown to 24px by a centred ::before — the same idiom `.x` uses.
accessibility.colour: The only coloured text is the plus/minus numeral pair (two-red law s151-D1) and the error title. Both declare `data-carries`, and the declaration is MEASURED at the browser rather than asserted: the numerals carry `label` (the minus sign is in the text), the error block carries `symbol label` (an error triangle plus a title).

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the search field, dropdown, segmented control, chip or link CSS instead of composing the existing atom — the #202 defect the Layer-2 brief names explicitly
Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded 2026-07-24
Copying date-range-picker's CALENDAR body into this bar — the bar owns the trigger and the presets; `Custom range…` hands off to the component that owns the calendar (edges.delegatesTo)
Giving the bar a fixed width — s210-D3 reserves that for the container
Disabling the controls while results load — a filter you cannot change while it is running is a trap; dim the chips, hold the count's position, keep every control live
Showing the previous count during loading or error as if it were current — loading shows a skeleton, error shows an em-dash
Selecting a filter state by colour alone — Dropdown's aria-selected, Segmented-control's aria-pressed and the chip's own label already carry the non-colour signal
Letting the bar decide its own state from the request it just made — the state is READ BACK off the consumer's data-apollo-result-state

$contract.$ruling: s258-D1 — cross-component wiring (filter->grid/KPI/chart) is the author's to write. s258-D2 — every interactive element is assumed to work, on rich seeded data.
$contract.$shape: An EVENT + ATTRIBUTE contract. A consumer imports nothing; it declares an attribute and, if it wants to, listens.

markers.data-apollo-filter-bar: on the bar root — marks the driver.
markers.data-apollo-filter-target: on the bar root, optional — a CSS selector for the consumer. Default: the first [data-apollo-filter-consumer] in the document.
markers.data-apollo-filter-consumer: on the consumer root — marks anything that renders a result set.

emits.detail: { query: string, filters: [{key, facet, value, label}], range: {preset, days, label}, view: string, density: string }

writes.data-apollo-view: written onto the consumer — so a CSS-only consumer can respond with no script at all.
writes.data-apollo-density: written onto the consumer — the same dial the bar applies to itself.

readsBack.data-apollo-result-count: the number matched, or "" while unknown
readsBack.data-apollo-result-total: the size of the unfiltered set
readsBack.data-apollo-result-state: ok | loading | empty | error — the bar moves its own data-ftb-state to match
readsBack.$why: The bar never assumes the answer to the question it just asked. A driver that reports success because it dispatched an event is the lying-state defect this contract exists to close.
